searchText: Hey all, has there been a discussion somewhere regarding JSON-RPC for EOF? For instance, what should `eth_getCode` return when called on an EOF contract? 🤔 <@403707149043105803> The same goes for 7702. Should it return the actual code, or the code it is delegated to? <@543900561460822016> I would assume that both would still return the raw bytecode of the contract though (and let downstream handlers of `eth_getCode` process it to return whatever the user expects) The Ethereum JSON-PRC spec contains an eth_getCode method, but it is not specified what is being retrieved Well, it says ``` eth_getCode Returns code at a given address. ``` So this is somewhat ambiguous for EOF I think The command eth_getCode returns the bytecode associated with the address in the Ethereum world state, that will be the deployed bytecode (or runtime bytecode) Right, so for EOF that should be the container? I guess so The init bytecode could be obtained from the deployment transaction's data field, unless it was created by a contract in which case you have to trace the transaction to obtain the details I think using eth_getCode to get the EOF code for an account is fine. The EVM doesn't have access to it, and clients/networks can always do something different as eth_getCode is outside of consensus. I think it should return the code that is actually present at the address, not the delegated code Cool, agree with both 😄

excerpts.content: Hey all, has there been a discussion somewhere regarding JSON-RPC for EOF? For instance, what should `eth_getCode` return when called on an EOF contract? 🤔 <@403707149043105803>

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: The same goes for 7702. Should it return the actual code, or the code it is delegated to? <@543900561460822016>

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: I would assume that both would still return the raw bytecode of the contract though (and let downstream handlers of `eth_getCode` process it to return whatever the user expects)

excerpts.author: empir.ether
excerpts.content: The Ethereum JSON-PRC spec contains an eth_getCode method, but it is not specified what is being retrieved

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content:
Well, it says 

```
eth_getCode
Returns code at a given address.
```

So this is somewhat ambiguous for EOF I think

excerpts.author: empir.ether
excerpts.content: The command eth_getCode returns the bytecode associated with the address in the Ethereum world state, that will be the deployed bytecode (or runtime bytecode)

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: Right, so for EOF that should be the container?

excerpts.author: empir.ether
excerpts.content: The init bytecode could be obtained from the deployment transaction's data field, unless it was created by a contract in which case you have to trace the transaction to obtain the details

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: I think using eth_getCode to get the EOF code for an account is fine.  The EVM doesn't have access to it, and clients/networks can always do something different as eth_getCode is outside of consensus.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: I think it should return the code that is actually present at the address, not the delegated code
